en.title: Lexicographically Largest Non-Increasing Array by Taking One and Skipping k
en.description:
Repeatedly choose one of the following: discard the current leftmost item; or append the current leftmost weight to the result and remove it together with the k items after it. If fewer than k items remain after it, they are all removed, and the current item can still be taken. The resulting weights must be non-increasing, and among all feasible results take the lexicographically largest: at the first difference the larger one wins, and when one sequence is a prefix of the other, the longer one wins.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n k; the second line contains the weights. The original text had no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤n≤200000, 0≤k≤10^9, 1≤weight≤10^9.
en.output: Output the result array, separated by spaces.
en.explanation: The answers are 5 3, 10 5 and 3. In the first example any number of prefix elements may be discarded; you are not limited to looking at the first k+1 items.
hints: Precompute the earliest index of the maximum in each suffix. Each round, take that maximum and continue from its index+k+1.
